external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches and may manually start a rebuild.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: The text does not specify the developer's trust zone or authentication details.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry used during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves dependencies, produces container images, publishes them, and calls the deploy controller.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of main by hand; that path is not reviewed.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Maintains the current release image SHA and responds to release queries from store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.
processes.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in each store's back office that runs the till software container and polls for releases.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office running the till software as a container.
processes.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it, or what it presents to the controller.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: The till software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

data_stores.name: git server
data_stores.description: The self-hosted repository containing developer branches, source, and the dependency lockfile.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: The registry storing container images tagged with commit SHA values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores. The registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: Developer pushes a branch to the git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: start build
data_flows.description: The git server starts a build after a merge to main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A merge to `main` is what starts a build.

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner resolves dependencies using the public package registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: publish image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.data_description: Container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: set current release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: Container image SHA and build authentication token

data_flows.name: query current release
data_flows.description: A store server asks the deploy controller which release is current.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current image from the image registry when its release differs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it pulls that image from the registry and restarts the container
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

data_flows.name: restart container
data_flows.description: The store server restarts the till software container after pulling a changed image.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it pulls that image from the registry and restarts the container

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually starts a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network hosting the git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate environment hosting the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The in-store estate containing the store servers and till software.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Build and deploy pipeline for the in-store estate.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public network reached during dependency resolution.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The corporate network is a network trust boundary because the text places components on it.
assumptions.basis: The git server and deploy controller are explicitly described as running on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The build environment is a network trust boundary because it is explicitly separate from the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The runner is described as living in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The store estate is a network trust boundary for the in-store servers.
assumptions.basis: The system is described as an in-store estate and the servers are located in each store's back office.

assumptions.assumption: The internet is a network trust boundary for the public package registry.
assumptions.basis: The public package registry is explicitly described as being on the internet.

assumptions.assumption: The git server holds business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: It holds developer branches, source, and the dependency lockfile used to build the till software.

assumptions.assumption: The image registry holds business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: It stores the container images used as releases for the store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The build runner handles business-critical data, credentials, and secrets.
assumptions.basis: It reads source and produces release images, and it uses the shared build token.

assumptions.assumption: The deploy controller handles business-critical data, credentials, and secrets.
assumptions.basis: It holds the current release record and accepts the shared build token.

assumptions.assumption: The store server handles business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: It pulls and runs the container image that constitutes the till software release.

assumptions.assumption: The till software handles business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: It is the till software deployed across the in-store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The publish-image flow carries business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries the finished container image used for the estate release.

assumptions.assumption: The set-current-release flow carries business-critical data, credentials, and secrets.
assumptions.basis: It carries the release image SHA and uses the shared build token.

assumptions.assumption: The query-current-release flow carries business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: It carries the current release image SHA.

assumptions.assumption: The pull-image flow carries business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: It carries the container image deployed to the store estate.
